title: How radio signals travel
blurb: The big idea before the cards.

lines.caption: A radio signal rarely takes just one path. Copies of it also bounce off buildings and hills.
lines.label: more than one path

lines.caption: Where the copies meet, they can add up or cancel. Move a few feet and the signal changes.
lines.label: stronger, weaker

lines.caption: Antennas work best when they are turned the same way. Cross them, and the signal gets weaker.
lines.label: match your antennas

lines.caption: Trees and rain soak up the shortest waves. Longer waves hardly notice them.
lines.label: absorbed on the way

lines.caption: And high above us, the ionosphere can reflect some radio waves back to the ground far away.
lines.label: back from the sky
